reason: Both correctly tell the homeowner to stop resetting the RCD, isolate the oven and call an engineer, and both correctly point to a heating element leaking to earth as it warms (though both say 'unplug' a hard-wired built-in rather than 'isolate at the cooker switch'). Conversation 1 stays consistent and clear: it explains why the delay-before-trip points to insulation breakdown on heating and firmly says this is engineer-only work. Conversation 2 offers a slightly richer differential (moisture after cleaning, terminal block) but then undermines its own stop-use message by proposing 'simple checks' including inspecting the element, which on a fan oven isn't visible without removing the back panel and which the customer won't do; the stuck-knob check is also irrelevant. Neither asked the useful RCD-vs-MCB, grill-only or smell/scorching questions, so the difference is modest.
